coverage_limits: OpenAlex stopped answering after the first query (the free daily budget shared by this IP was used up), so journal sweeps ran on Crossref instead; Crossref ranks by loose relevance, caps each sweep at 100 rows per journal, and carries no abstracts for Elsevier, ASME, most Springer and Taylor & Francis items, so some relevant titles in high-volume journals (Automation in Construction, Buildings, AEI) may sit below the cutoff. Semantic Scholar's search endpoint was rate-limited, so citation chasing used only seven seed papers. Springer, Taylor & Francis and CumInCAD pages blocked scripts; nine records were kept on title and venue alone because no abstract could be retrieved (flagged in their evidence), and CAADRIA/eCAADe/ACADIA papers were screened on titles only. Saturation was not reached: the last passes still turned up occasional design-education experiments in non-design journals (TSC, ETR&D, EAIT, Frontiers, JCAL), so education- and HCI-adjacent venues and Chinese- or Korean-language design journals are covered only partly. HCI venue tool studies (CHI, C&C, UIST) were kept only when the task was design ideation.

candidates.title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence in Conceptual Design: An Large Language Model–Powered Framework to Enhance Originality and Credibility
candidates.task: conceptual design challenges (design engineering)
candidates.evidence: Design-engineering participants solved one of three design challenges with GPT-4 without explanations (n=39) or with an explainable-AI LLM framework (n=39); 10 separate raters scored usefulness, feasibility, originality and credibility. The XAI condition raised originality and credibility (88 participants in total including raters; random assignment not stated in the abstract).

candidates.title: Real-time dynamic graph construction and reasoning to support human-AI collaborative product conceptual design
candidates.task: product conceptual design on an interactive whiteboard
candidates.evidence: User study (N=24) compared an LLM-based real-time graph reasoning whiteboard with a chat-only AI baseline (AI-configuration comparison); the structured approach improved the engineering quality of final design schemes.

candidates.title: An LLM-based multi-agent system to assist early-stage product design and evaluation
candidates.task: early-stage product design (UAV landing gear)
candidates.evidence: Mostly a system evaluation (104 simulated design sessions), plus a user study comparing the LLM multi-agent DesignAgent with a baseline system that reports higher design accuracy and solution quality; human sample size not given in the abstract and outcomes are quality rather than novelty.

candidates.title: AI-Assisted Bio-Inspired Design: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Directed Intuition in Large Language Model Outputs
candidates.task: bio-inspired design solutions
candidates.evidence: 2x2x2 factorial comparing LLM-generated and human-generated design solutions (participant type x 'consider nature' instruction x problem); directing the LLM raised novelty and variety, but the LLM still produced fewer novel ideas than humans; no human-LLM difference in variety and quality.

candidates.title: stickynexus: Leveraging Sticky Note Interactions to Improve Information Management in Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Design
candidates.task: creative design with GenAI information (sticky-note interface)
candidates.evidence: User study (N=18) of a sticky-note interface for organizing GenAI output during design; reports better exploration of information and creative exploration. The comparison condition and whether creativity was rated on outputs are not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: StepIdeator: Utilizing Mixed Representations to Support Step-By-Step Design With Generative Artificial Intelligence
candidates.task: product conceptual design with mixed representations
candidates.evidence: Comparative study (N=16) of StepIdeator, a step-by-step GenAI design tool, against a baseline; reports improved idea externalization and enhanced creativity (AI-configuration comparison; scoring details not in the abstract).

candidates.title: Multi-PDAI: integrating multimodal GenAI models for participatory design
candidates.task: participatory design of a wheeled humanoid robot
candidates.evidence: Crossover experiment (8 designers, 16 users) comparing a multimodal GenAI participatory-design platform (Multi-PDAI) with Stable Diffusion; 10 industry experts rated the platform's generated images as more innovative and aesthetically appealing.

candidates.title: Generative re-creation of architectural styles: a co-evolutionary framework based on human-AI bidirectional feedback loops
candidates.task: architectural style re-creation (Zaha Hadid case)
candidates.evidence: Designers working within a co-evolutionary human-AI framework produced proposals rated higher on functional rationality, structural credibility and environmental responsiveness than prompt-engineering and style-model-adaptation baselines (AI-configuration comparison; sample size and assignment not stated).

candidates.title: A foundation model enhanced approach for generative design in combinational creativity
candidates.authors: Chen, Zhang, Han, Sun, Childs, Wang
candidates.task: combinational creativity idea generation
candidates.evidence: Proposes a foundation-model approach to combinational ideas; an experiment scored ideas generated with and without the foundation model, and a user study compared the CombinatorX tool with an existing combinational creativity tool and internet search on idea-generation effectiveness.

candidates.title: The study of human-AI Co-creation design under generative artificial intelligence: cognition, process, method, and outcome
candidates.task: review of human-AI co-creation in conceptual design
candidates.evidence: Systematic review with CiteSpace bibliometrics of 80 publications on human-AI co-creation design under generative AI (cognition, process, method, outcome); notes an indirect influence of generative AI on design outcomes. Not a meta-analysis.

candidates.title: Integrating AIGC with design: dependence, application, and evolution - a systematic literature review
candidates.task: review of AIGC in the design process
candidates.evidence: PRISMA systematic review of 90 documents on AIGC in design, covering its role in creative divergence, design generation, advice and evaluation; descriptive, not a meta-analysis of creativity effects.

candidates.title: Impact of image-generation tool on designers’ cognitive styles and design performance during product conceptual design
candidates.task: product conceptual design with an image-generation tool
candidates.evidence: Title indicates an experiment on how an image-generation tool affects designers' cognitive styles and design performance in product conceptual design; abstract not retrieved in this run, so conditions and outcome scoring are unconfirmed.

candidates.title: Do Large Language Models Produce Diverse Design Concepts? A Comparative Study with Human-Crowdsourced Solutions
candidates.venue: Journal of Computing and Information Science in Engineering 25(2), 024501
candidates.task: design solutions for five design topics
candidates.evidence: GPT-4 generated 4,000 design solutions under different parameters and prompting techniques; diversity metrics compared with 100 human-crowdsourced solutions per topic. Human-generated solutions were consistently more diverse.

candidates.title: ConceptVis: Exploring and Visualizing Design Concepts With Large Language Models Using Interactive Knowledge Graph
candidates.venue: Journal of Computing and Information Science in Engineering 26(1), 011002
candidates.task: early-stage concept generation
candidates.evidence: User study with 24 novice designers comparing ConceptVis (LLM with interactive knowledge graph) against a chat-based LLM interface; reports less repetitive concept generation, less fixation on early ideas and improved efficiency and quality of concepts.

candidates.title: Influence of Artificial Intelligence Use on Creativity-Related Perceptions and Outcomes in an Idea Generation Task
candidates.venue: Journal of Computing and Information Science in Engineering 26(8), 081005
candidates.task: speculative design idea generation (Futures Wheel)
candidates.evidence: Already-collected item, reported to link versions: professional engineers and designers in three groups produced 120 ideas fully human, with AI-as-tool, or fully AI-generated; experts rated well-craftedness, usefulness and novelty, and cosine similarity showed AI-generated ideas covered a smaller design space. The IDETC 2025 paper 'Influence of AI Use on Creativity in a Speculative Design Process' is the earlier conference version.

candidates.title: An Large Language Model-Augmented Method to Assist Novice Designers in Divergent Thinking
candidates.venue: Journal of Computing and Information Science in Engineering 25(9), 091001
candidates.task: Alternative Uses Test and conceptual design tasks
candidates.evidence: Tests an LLM-augmented divergent-thinking method for novice designers with the AUT and conceptual design tasks; reports that LLM support raised fluency, flexibility and originality of divergent-thinking outcomes (comparison condition and assignment not detailed in the abstract).

candidates.title: Understanding the Impact of Applying Large Language Model in Engineering Design Education
candidates.venue: Journal of Computing and Information Science in Engineering 25(2), 021008
candidates.task: mechanical engineering design course: concept generation and CAD modeling
candidates.evidence: Compared AI-assisted (ChatGPT-3.5) student groups with groups without AI; AI broadened the diversity of generated concepts but introduced a bias toward existing popular designs. Assignment method and sample size not given in the abstract.

candidates.title: Analogical reasoning with large language models: a co-creative framework and benchmarking of LLMs in design ideation
candidates.task: design ideation with LLM-generated analogical stimuli
candidates.evidence: Controlled ideation experiments with 24 undergraduate design students: groups assisted by an LLM analogical-stimuli support tool generated higher-rated ideas than unassisted groups; the paper also benchmarks LLMs on analogical tasks.

candidates.title: How generative AI supports human in conceptual design
candidates.authors: Chen, Song, Guo, Sun, Childs, Yin
candidates.task: two conceptual design tasks (novice designers)
candidates.evidence: Novice designers completed two design tasks with or without text-to-text and text-to-image GenAI; expert ratings and process analysis show GenAI mainly helped problem definition and idea generation. N=20 comes from a search snippet of the arXiv PDF, not the abstract.

candidates.title: Prompting for products: investigating design space exploration strategies for text-to-image generative models
candidates.authors: Chong, Lo, Rayan, Dow, Ahmed, Lykourentzou
candidates.task: product image generation with a text-to-image model
candidates.evidence: Relates participants' prompting strategies in a text-to-image tool (mono vs multi-criteria prompts, goal orientation, global vs local editing) to feasibility, novelty and aesthetics of the product images; strategies were observed, not assigned, and there is no no-AI arm.

candidates.title: “Who” designs better? A competition among human, artificial intelligence and human–AI collaboration
candidates.task: light fixture design for a pediatric waiting room
candidates.evidence: Design competition among AI, a human designer and human-AI collaboration; MTurk and Prolific workers rated sketches, 3D renderings and VR models with the Creative Product Semantic Scale.

candidates.title: The effects of generative AI model type and visual stimuli type on design creativity
candidates.venue: Artificial Intelligence for Engineering Design, Analysis and Manufacturing 39, e17
candidates.task: early-stage design ideation in design education
candidates.evidence: Controlled experiment varying generative AI tool type and visual stimulus type; text-to-image tools and abstract visual stimuli enhanced design creativity in divergent and convergent processes, with a warning about design fixation. Sample size and assignment not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: Enhancing designer creativity through human–AI co-ideation: a co-creation framework for design ideation with custom GPT
candidates.venue: Artificial Intelligence for Engineering Design, Analysis and Manufacturing 39, e22
candidates.task: industrial design ideation with a custom GPT (Co-Ideator)
candidates.evidence: After a designer survey, a design case study compared ideation with a custom-GPT co-ideation framework against traditional ideation and a non-AI condition; novelty and quality of ideation were higher with the custom GPT.

candidates.title: Creative potential of image-generative AI models for conceptual engineering design tasks
candidates.venue: Artificial Intelligence for Engineering Design, Analysis and Manufacturing 40, e8
candidates.task: conceptual engineering design task (image generation vs students)
candidates.evidence: Six image-generative AI tools and 20 design engineering students addressed the same task; outputs compared on quantity, variety, novelty and quality. AI produced many solutions quickly but with less diversity, novelty and quality than the students.

candidates.title: A novel idea generation tool using a structured conversational AI (CAI) system
candidates.venue: Artificial Intelligence for Engineering Design, Analysis and Manufacturing 39, e11
candidates.task: idea generation for product design problems
candidates.evidence: 30 novice product designers generated ideas with traditional methods and with an LLM conversational ideation interface; an expert panel judged the AI-supported ideas more prolific, novel and diverse (fluency, novelty, variety).

candidates.title: ChatGPT as an inventor: eliciting the strengths and weaknesses of current large language models against humans in engineering design
candidates.venue: Artificial Intelligence for Engineering Design, Analysis and Manufacturing 39, e6
candidates.task: 48-hour prototyping hackathon (engineering design)
candidates.evidence: ChatGPT-4 led a team (two participants executed its instructions) against graduate engineering student teams; compares design practices and performance across more than 100 prototypes. The LLM placed second of six, generated concepts well, and showed design fixation.

candidates.title: Switching Perspectives: Enhancing Generative Artificial Intelligence's Creativity, by Humans, With Design
candidates.task: egg task (creative design problem)
candidates.evidence: Expert interviews generated hypotheses, then an egg-task experiment compared ideation with and without GenAI tools; GenAI users generated more ideas, GenAI did not prevent fixation but supported exploration and second-order defixation.

candidates.title: Generative AI-enhanced human-AI collaborative conceptual design: A systematic literature review
candidates.task: review of GenAI in human-AI collaborative conceptual design
candidates.evidence: Systematic literature review of generative-AI-enhanced human-AI collaborative conceptual design (from title and venue; abstract not retrieved in this run).

candidates.title: Inspiration or indication? Evaluating the qualities of design inspiration boards created using text to image generative AI
candidates.task: design inspiration boards
candidates.evidence: Evaluative study comparing inspiration boards made with image-generative AI and with traditional methods on diversity, quantity, fidelity and ambiguity; AI boards held more images but less diversity. Whether boards were made by assigned participants is not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: AI vs. human: exploring the potential of generative AI as a feedback tool to support ideation in design education
candidates.task: brainstorming phase in design education (feedback on ideas)
candidates.evidence: Controlled study with 25 students comparing GPT-4 feedback with feedback from six human educators during brainstorming; reports effects on motivation and iterative idea refinement. Rated creativity of ideas is not explicit in the abstract.

candidates.title: AI as an element to overcome creative fixation in design teams
candidates.task: team problem framing, ideation and concept exploration workshop
candidates.evidence: Creative ideation workshop with design-student teams examining whether GenAI helps teams overcome creative fixation, looking at team dynamics and creative results; whether a no-AI comparison group was used is not clear from the abstract.

candidates.title: Design and evaluation of an AI-based application to enhance creativity in design thinking workshops
candidates.task: design thinking workshop ideation
candidates.evidence: Compared only-human teams with human-AI teams using an AI ideation application; AI teams generated fewer ideas, while AI improved the usability of ideas in the divergent phase and helped converge on more novel ideas.

candidates.title: AI-powered inventive design: idea funnelling, concept creation, and hybrid problem-solving teams
candidates.task: inventive engineering design problems (idea funnelling)
candidates.evidence: Comparative experiments on AI-powered idea funnelling with ChatGPT and Gemini and on hybrid AI-human problem-solving teams, judged on feasibility, contextual relevance and innovation quality; the human comparison design is unclear from the abstract.

candidates.title: Neurocognitive assessment of generative AI on designers’ creative cognition: evidence from biologically inspired design tasks
candidates.authors: Shrivastava, Sharma, Dabas, Mukherjee, Cascini, Keshwani
candidates.task: bio-inspired design tasks
candidates.evidence: 30 designers worked with bio-inspired stimuli in three modes (BID only, ChatGPT only, BID plus ChatGPT); creativity was indexed with EEG task-related power for divergent and convergent thinking, not with ratings of the designs.

candidates.title: EXPLORING THE IMPACT OF GENERATIVE STIMULI ON THE CREATIVITY OF DESIGNERS IN COMBINATIONAL DESIGN
candidates.task: combinational design ideation with visual stimuli
candidates.evidence: 20 designers used GAN-generated combinational stimuli and ordinary combinational image stimuli in two design tasks; reports an advantage of generative stimuli for creativity of ideation outcomes, partly based on participants' self-evaluation.

candidates.title: Stimulating design ideation with artificial intelligence: present and (short-term) future
candidates.task: review of AI support for design inspiration and ideation
candidates.evidence: Review of contributions on AI support for design stimulation and ideation with a proposed framework; notes most contributions are demonstrative. Narrative review, not a meta-analysis.

candidates.title: Understanding ChatGPT’s impact on student-team ideation outcomes for new product development
candidates.task: student-team ideation for new product development (associative thinking)
candidates.evidence: Two workshops: ChatGPT-assisted team ideation (n=22) versus analogue methods (n=17) in a 24-minute session; the analogue group produced over twice as many ideas and slightly more flexible and original ideas.

candidates.title: EXPLORING CHATGPT’S IMPACT ON STUDENT-TEAM IDEATION OUTCOMES FOR NEW PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT: A PILOT STUDY
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the International Conference on Engineering and Product Design Education (EPDE 2024), 533-538
candidates.task: student-team ideation for new product development (Post-it ideas)
candidates.evidence: Pilot with 35 undergraduates in two innovation workshops, one using ChatGPT for associative-thinking team ideation and one analogue; fluency and flexibility were slightly lower and originality markedly lower in the ChatGPT group.

candidates.title: Case study: is there a space for TRIZ in the era of ChatGPT?
candidates.task: industrial product development problem (TRIZ)
candidates.evidence: Industrial case study comparing solutions generated by a human team with solutions from LLMs and TRIZ-enhanced LLMs. Distinct from the already-collected Čok (2026) TRIZ experiment.

candidates.title: INFLUENCE OF IMAGE STIMULI ON DESIGN CREATIVITY: EXPLORATION OF GENERATIVE AI IN GROUP IDEATION
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the International Conference on Engineering and Product Design Education (EPDE 2025), 19-24
candidates.task: group ideation with collaborative sketching in a design course
candidates.evidence: After group sketch ideation, each participant got a tailored AI-generated image stimulus; external evaluators rated novelty and usefulness of the 18 best ideas and traced their inspiration sources, finding a minimal role for the AI images. No no-AI comparison group.

candidates.title: Text Stimuli Created by Generative AI in Ideation: An Exploratory Study
candidates.task: ideation with GenAI-created text stimuli
candidates.evidence: Exploratory study of text stimuli created by generative AI in ideation; reports an impact on idea generation, mostly from participants' reflections. Conditions and scoring not described in the abstract.

candidates.title: IS HIGH SKETCHING PROFICIENCY STILL AN ADVANTAGE? EXPLORING THE ROLE OF FREEHAND DRAWING IN VEHICLE DESIGN WITHIN THE 2D GENERATIVE AI LANDSCAPE
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the International Conference on Engineering and Product Design Education (EPDE 2025), 739-744
candidates.task: mini-mobility vehicle design (sketching vs GenAI)
candidates.evidence: Untrained students and trained sketching experts tackled a vehicle design challenge with GenAI tools; an expert panel compared 2D freehand sketches with GenAI alternatives; largely auto-ethnographic.

candidates.title: HOW CAN AI SUPPORT THE CREATION OF NOVEL IDEAS IN PRODUCT DESIGN
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the International Conference on Engineering and Product Design Education (EPDE 2024), 133-138
candidates.task: 6-3-5 ideation for a kitchen product for arthritis sufferers
candidates.evidence: Students in a 6-3-5 workshop could use ChatGPT, Google, or no support (control); novelty of the outputs was analyzed and AI-supported ideas were more novel than control ideas.

candidates.title: Conceptual Design Generation Using Large Language Models
candidates.venue: Proceedings of ASME IDETC-CIE 2023, Volume 6: 35th International Conference on Design Theory and Methodology (DTM), V006T06A021
candidates.task: solutions to 12 design problems (LLM vs crowdsourcing)
candidates.evidence: LLM-generated solutions to 12 design problems compared with crowdsourced human solutions via expert ratings and computational metrics; LLM solutions had higher feasibility and usefulness, crowdsourced solutions more novelty.

candidates.title: An Empirical Study Measuring the Effects of Generative AI on Early-Stage Engineering Design and Neurocognition
candidates.venue: Proceedings of ASME IDETC-CIE 2025, Volume 4: 37th International Conference on Design Theory and Methodology (DTM), V004T06A048
candidates.task: two-stage sustainable site redevelopment design task
candidates.evidence: 60 engineering students identified design constraints either with generative AI or unaided, then all developed concepts without AI; the AI group found more constraints and later, without AI, produced more sustainability-related concepts; brain imaging showed reduced effort.

candidates.title: A Study of the Exploratory Creativity Performance Between Machine and Human Designers
candidates.authors: Yin, Qin, Liu, Childs, Sun, Chen
candidates.venue: Proceedings of ASME IDETC-CIE 2022, Volume 6: 34th International Conference on Design Theory and Methodology (DTM), V006T06A001
candidates.task: exploratory creativity imagery (DALL-E vs novice designers)
candidates.evidence: DALL-E-generated imagery compared with novice designers' imagery; expert designers rated creativity and exploratory creativity. Humans scored higher on creativity, the model higher on exploratory creativity.

candidates.title: Emotional valence and arousal: the impact of AI-generated image stimuli on design creativity
candidates.venue: International Journal of Technology and Design Education 35(3), 1103-1122
candidates.task: design tasks with AI-generated inspirational images
candidates.evidence: Two experiments varied the emotional valence (positive, neutral, negative) and arousal of AI-generated inspirational images, and problem type, and measured design creativity; all arms used AI images (AI-variant comparison).

candidates.title: Effectiveness of generative AI in higher education design pedagogy: a meta-analysis of usage modes
candidates.venue: International Journal of Technology and Design Education (online first)
candidates.task: meta-analysis of GenAI usage modes in higher-education design pedagogy
candidates.evidence: Meta-analysis of the effectiveness of generative AI usage modes in higher-education design pedagogy (title); abstract not retrieved in this run, so whether creativity outcomes are pooled is unconfirmed.

candidates.title: Investigating generative artificial intelligence’s role in logo design pedagogy: effects on learning experience and outcomes
candidates.venue: International Journal of Technology and Design Education (online first)
candidates.task: logo design conceptualization (graphic design students)
candidates.evidence: Compared GAI-assisted and traditional teaching during logo concept ideation for novice and skilled students; GAI raised quantity, novelty and diversity of concepts but had limited effect on design quality. Assignment method not stated.

candidates.title: Product design education: integration with artificial intelligence as one of the tools for increasing creativity
candidates.venue: International Journal of Technology and Design Education 36(2), 685-705
candidates.task: product design education
candidates.evidence: Compared an AI-integrated instruction group with a conventional group in product design education; the AI group showed a significantly larger creativity gain. Measures appear partly survey-based (summary of the abstract).

candidates.title: Can artificial intelligence support creativity in early design processes?
candidates.task: urban furniture design tasks (design students)
candidates.evidence: 40 design students randomly assigned to two groups; in phase 1 one group used a text-to-image tool, in phase 2 both worked without AI. Professionals rated outcomes with the Creative Product Semantic Scale (novelty, resolution, elaboration); the AI group scored higher in both phases (authors call it quasi-experimental).

candidates.title: The impact of generative AI on architectural design education: insights from hands-on experience with architecture students
candidates.task: supervised architecture design project
candidates.evidence: Architecture students at KFUPM in a GenAI test group versus a control group were assessed on creativity, time efficiency and design quality; the test group performed better, with a 14 percent gain in design form and aesthetics.

candidates.title: Generative AI as a cognitive support tool in early-stage design ideation: A human–AI co-ideation experiment
candidates.task: early-stage design ideation brief (design students)
candidates.evidence: Counterbalanced within-subjects experiment with 32 design students: text-and-image AI-assisted workflow versus human-only brainstorming; expert ratings favored AI outputs on problem framing and mechanism but human-only outputs on innovation and solution strategies.

candidates.title: A Study on the Role of Midjourney, A Generative Artificial Intelligence Tool, in Enhancing Student Creativity in Illustration Design Classes
candidates.venue: Journal of Computer Assisted Learning 42(5), e70305
candidates.task: illustration design studio (undergraduates)
candidates.evidence: Parallel-group two-section quasi-experiment: Midjourney-based ideation workflow (n=82) versus conventional non-generative workflow (n=80); baseline-adjusted final creativity and originality rubric scores were higher in the AI section. The study framed homogenisation as a concern to control.

candidates.title: AI-generated inspiration for the design process: effects across the vividness of visual imagery spectrum
candidates.venue: International Journal of Design Creativity and Innovation 14(3), 171-189
candidates.task: wireframe prototype design (nonprofessionals)
candidates.evidence: Nonprofessionals created wireframe prototypes with or without AI-generated sample designs for inspiration; quality, accuracy, time and user experience were compared, moderated by vividness of visual imagery; findings on quality were mixed.

candidates.title: From designer to curator: cognitive and creative trade-offs in GenAI-assisted design
candidates.task: digital textile pattern design
candidates.evidence: Within-subject study: 34 students did matched pattern tasks with conventional vector tools and with GenAI in Illustrator; GenAI lowered workload but outputs got lower creativity and aesthetic ratings, and breadth of distinct ideas did not increase (stylistic convergence).

candidates.title: Comparative Study of Generative AI and Traditional Tools for Evaluating Creativity and Efficiency in UI/UX Desig
candidates.venue: International Journal of Innovations in Science and Technology (2026), 924
candidates.task: UI/UX design task (novice and expert designers)
candidates.evidence: Novice and expert designers created UI/UX designs with Galileo AI or with Figma; creativity (Creative Product Semantic Scale), NASA-TLX and completion time were compared between AI and traditional groups.

candidates.title: Exploring creativity in human–AI co-creation: a comparative study across design experience
candidates.task: design process comparison across design experience
candidates.evidence: Comparative experiment of a human-AI co-creative design process versus the traditional design process; creative performance was higher with the co-creative process, mainly idea generation for novices and quality for experienced designers.

candidates.title: A structured Kano-AHP framework for AI-assisted generative media production: experimental evidence from short-form animation design
candidates.task: AI-assisted short-form animation production
candidates.evidence: 20 practitioners made anime-style clips with generative AI under a baseline or a structured Kano-AHP workflow; experts and 60 viewers rated narrative coherence, style consistency, expressiveness and quality higher for the structured workflow. AI-workflow comparison, not AI versus no AI.

candidates.title: Integrating Generative Artificial Intelligence and Human Design: The Impact of Automation Level on Human Creative Experience and Efficiency
candidates.task: design task with a generative design tool at three automation levels
candidates.evidence: Single-factor between-subjects experiment (79 participants) varying the automation level of a generative AI design tool (low, moderate, high); outcomes were time, creative experience and creative quality (aesthetics, usability).

candidates.title: Assimilating generative AI into ideation work: seeding, search and human contribution
candidates.task: professional idea generation with GenAI seeding configurations
candidates.evidence: 400 professionals in four configurations: human-only, unstructured human-GenAI collaboration, GenAI seeding, and a TC-based GenAI configuration; experts rated novelty, utility and feasibility, and only the TC-based configuration raised novelty. Assignment method not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: From Manual Ideation to AI-Augmented Exploration: Evaluating Human–AI Workflows in Furniture Design Education (A Quasi-Experimental Study)
candidates.task: furniture design (interior design students)
candidates.evidence: Pre/post quasi-experiment: 34 students did a manual design activity and then an AI-assisted redesign (Vizcom, Krea.ai, ChatGPT); 27 completers; Creativity Support Index exploration rose and expert jurors rated the designs.

candidates.title: Uncovering the effect of Gen AI-assisted learning on students’ creativity: A meta-analysis from quasi-experimental evidence
candidates.task: meta-analysis of GenAI-assisted learning and creativity
candidates.evidence: Meta-analysis of quasi-experimental evidence on generative-AI-assisted learning and students' creativity (title); abstract not retrieved in this run.

candidates.title: Comparing AIGC and traditional idea generation methods: Evaluating their impact on creativity in the product design ideation phase
candidates.authors: Lin, Jiang, Deng, Bian, Fang, Zhu
candidates.task: product design ideation phase
candidates.evidence: Title indicates a comparison of AIGC-based and traditional idea generation methods and their effect on creativity in product design ideation; abstract not retrieved in this run, so design and N are unconfirmed.

candidates.title: Enhancing human computer collaboration in design process: How AI-generated content elevates students’ creativity
candidates.task: design process with AI-generated content (students)
candidates.evidence: Title indicates a study of how AI-generated content raises students' creativity in the design process; abstract not retrieved in this run, so whether an AI vs no-AI comparison exists is unconfirmed.

candidates.title: Evaluating the impact of AIGC-Supported design ideation on Designers’ cognitive load and creativity
candidates.task: two-stage design challenge (ideation and concept development)
candidates.evidence: Controlled experiment with three assistance modes (AI-supported collaboration, designer-to-designer collaboration, image-stimulus support); CPSS novelty and resolution trended higher with AIGC during ideation, and AIGC raised novelty and elaboration in development.

candidates.title: The influence of artificial intelligence generated content-based problem-solving on engineering students’ creativity: a controlled experimental study
candidates.task: engineering creative problem-solving course
candidates.evidence: Two-month controlled study: AIGC group (n=54) versus traditional-methods group (n=59), apparently intact groups; Creative Engineering Design Assessment fluency, flexibility, originality and usefulness improved only in the AIGC group.

candidates.title: Enhancing design ldeation: comparing AIGC-engaged and traditional brainstorming in educational contexts
candidates.task: industrial design brainstorming
candidates.evidence: Controlled experiment with 21 industrial design students: AIGC-engaged brainstorming versus traditional brainstorming; outputs rated on novelty, feasibility, correlation and utility, with AIGC higher on novelty, feasibility and correlation.

candidates.title: EEG assessment of artificial intelligence-generated content impact on student creative performance and neurophysiological states in product design
candidates.task: intelligent walking cane product design task
candidates.evidence: 64 third-year design students randomly assigned to AIGC tools (ChatGPT, Midjourney, Stable Diffusion) or traditional design software for a 3-hour design task; creative performance (originality, novelty, elegance, relevance) was higher with AIGC (d = 0.55); EEG concentration also higher.

candidates.title: A Comparative Study of Design Ideation between Generative AI and Product Designers: Creativity, Innovation, and Empathy
candidates.task: 'Smart Home AI Robot' design challenge
candidates.evidence: Three groups with different reliance on generative AI (AI, designers, AI-designer collaboration) tackled the same challenge; experts rated creativity, empathy and innovation, and the collaborative group scored highest. Crossref lists the authors twice (bilingual record).

candidates.title: An Exploratory Experiment Using ChatGPT in the Idea Generation Process for Product-Service System
candidates.task: product-service system ideation (healthcare wearables)
candidates.evidence: Two teams of four designers ideated for four hours with conventional methods or with generative AI (ChatGPT-4, Bard); the AI team produced about 1.67 times as many ideas, with expert-rated creativity on par.

candidates.title: Enhancing Creative Confidence in Design Students Through Topology‐Preserving AI Scaffolding
candidates.venue: International Journal of Art & Design Education (online first), e70040
candidates.task: early-stage spatial concept ideation (design students)
candidates.evidence: Controlled experiment comparing a topology-preserving ControlNet sketch-scaffold workflow with static moodboard ideation; blind experts rated line-art outcomes, and the AI group had higher overall design quality (d = 0.88). Sample size missing from the retrieved abstract.

candidates.title: Exploring the Cognitive Reconstruction Mechanism of Generative AI in Outcome-Based Design Education: A Study on Load Optimization and Performance Impact Based on Dual-Path Teaching
candidates.authors: Dong, He, Li, Wang, Lu, Yang
candidates.task: undergraduate design education (dual-path teaching)
candidates.evidence: Compared an AI-assisted path (DeepSeek LLM with critical reconstruction behaviours) with a traditional path; the AI path scored higher on design quality (72.43 vs 65.60), analyzed with cognitive-load mediation models.

candidates.title: AI Sparring in Conceptual Architectural Design: A Systematic Review of Generative AI as a Pedagogical Partner (2015–2025)
candidates.authors: Stanimirovic, Momcilovic Petronijevic, Stoiljkovic, Kondic, Nikolic
candidates.task: review of GenAI in architectural design education
candidates.evidence: PRISMA systematic review of 40 papers on generative AI in architectural design education; reports more creative output but less reflective engagement when AI replaces early ideation.

candidates.title: Generative artificial intelligence in creative contexts: a systematic review and future research agenda
candidates.task: review of GenAI in creative contexts
candidates.evidence: Systematic literature review of 64 studies on generative AI in creative contexts, including implications for creative outcomes; not a meta-analysis.

candidates.title: How does contextual fidelity impact how we think, talk, and act in AI-assisted engineering design?
candidates.task: AI-assisted engineering design
candidates.evidence: Title indicates an experiment on how the contextual fidelity of AI assistance changes how designers think, talk and act in engineering design; abstract not retrieved, so creativity outcomes are unknown.

candidates.title: Reshaping team collaboration and creativity in co-design: the role of large language models
candidates.task: co-design team collaboration with LLMs
candidates.evidence: Title indicates a study of how LLMs reshape team collaboration and creativity in co-design; abstract not retrieved, design unknown.

candidates.title: GenAI and Search Tools in Design Education: Comparative Analysis of Student Creativity, Outcomes, and Experiences
candidates.venue: Human Factors in Training, Education, and Learning Sciences (AHFE 2026), AHFE International 231, 141-149
candidates.task: industrial design ideation (no tool vs Pinterest vs Midjourney)
candidates.evidence: 45 industrial design undergraduates randomly assigned to no tool, Pinterest image search, or Midjourney; 10 experts rated outputs on effectiveness, originality, usability and feasibility. Midjourney fostered originality; search improved feasibility but raised homogenization and imitation risks. Author order taken from the PDF (Crossref lists Xia, Jin, Qi).

candidates.title: A Comparative Study on the Impact of AIGC and Traditional Inspiration Sources on the Design Process of Designers
candidates.venue: Creativity, Innovation and Entrepreneurship (AHFE 2025), AHFE International 166
candidates.task: design ideation inspiration search (Midjourney vs Pinterest)
candidates.evidence: 12 design master's students ideated with Midjourney or Pinterest as inspiration sources; think-aloud protocols and interviews suggest AIGC supported associative search and more unique design solutions (process-oriented outcomes).

candidates.title: The impact of Midjourney on students’ design and design process: an exploratory study
candidates.venue: Designing Retail & Services Futures Colloquium 2025 (Design Research Society)
candidates.task: retail design exercise (master's students, three cohorts)
candidates.evidence: Three yearly cohorts did the same retail design exercise with Midjourney introduced at different phases or not at all; the cohort using it in concept development showed more creativity and storytelling but no effect on innovativeness or originality.

candidates.title: Empirical Study of Problem-solution Co-evolution in Human-GAI Collaborative Conceptual Design
candidates.task: conceptual design co-creation with GAI
candidates.evidence: Retrospective protocol analysis of 20 novice designers co-designing with text-to-text and text-to-image generative AI, combined with creativity assessments; argues GAI can amplify team creativity. No explicit no-AI comparison in the abstract.

candidates.title: The Effect of Generative AI on Design Students' Critical Thinking and Creative Achievement
candidates.task: graphic poster design (traditional tools vs Midjourney/DALL-E)
candidates.evidence: Counterbalanced within-subjects experiment: 61 students randomly assigned to order (traditional tools then AI tools, or the reverse), two weeks apart; blind expert ratings of the posters were higher with AI, while self-reported critical thinking was lower.

candidates.title: The Impact of AI Tools on Team Creativity: An Empirical Study in a Design Education Setting
candidates.task: team design workshop (AI at ideation vs storyboarding stage)
candidates.evidence: Workshop comparison of design-student teams using AI at the ideation stage versus at the concept storyboarding stage; Creativity Support Index and process data suggest AI at ideation raised idea diversity and lowered load (largely self-reported).

candidates.title: Ideasquares: Utilizing generative text as a source of design inspiration
candidates.task: design ideation with generated concept texts vs conventional search
candidates.evidence: Comparative user study where young designers ideated with a text-generation model fine-tuned on Red Dot winners (generative querying mode) versus a conventional search mode; findings are mainly qualitative about how generated texts are reinterpreted.

candidates.title: Generative AI Makes Creative Output More Homogeneous
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 European Conference on Cognitive Ergonomics (ECCE 2026), 198-201
candidates.task: meta-analysis of homogenization in human-AI co-creation
candidates.evidence: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 19 studies (61 effect sizes) on homogenization in human-AI co-creation; finds a small significant homogenization effect of AI use (d = 0.334). Possibly a short version of the already-collected de Rooij (2026) homogenisation meta-analysis.

candidates.title: Human-AI Co-Creation in Visual Communication Design: A Framework and Empirical Study
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Generative Design, 77-80
candidates.task: poster design brief (professional visual designers)
candidates.evidence: Empirical study with professional visual designers on one poster brief examining how AI participation affects efficiency, creative exploration and visual quality; reports faster prototyping and wider idea generation as trend-level evidence from a small sample.

candidates.title: Co-Constructed or Constrained? How AI Collaboration Tools Reshape UI Design Practice in a Time-Boxed Design Challenge
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems, 1-27
candidates.task: high-fidelity UI design tasks (FigmaAI vs no AI)
candidates.evidence: Within-subject study with 16 professional UX designers, each doing one UI task with FigmaAI and one without; AI constrained exploration and produced designs that were more visually and structurally similar.

candidates.title: InspirationGraph for Progressive Design Space Exploration
candidates.authors: Ling, Xiao, Zhou, Ma, Wei, Leung
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems, 1-23
candidates.task: product design ideation with a structured text-to-image tool
candidates.evidence: User study with 24 participants of InspirationGraph, a structured T2I exploration tool; reports support for divergent thinking and lower cognitive load. Comparison condition and output scoring not described in the abstract.

candidates.title: Reviving Reflection-in-Action: Instilling Designerly Thinking in AI-Supported Ideation through Multimodal Prompting
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Creativity and Cognition (C&C 2026), 359-376
candidates.task: design ideation with an AI creativity support tool (text vs sketch prompts)
candidates.evidence: Within-participants study with design students comparing text, sketch, and sketch-plus-tags prompting in an AI creativity support tool; the sketch modality tended to raise fluency, with inconclusive differences in variety, originality and quality.

candidates.title: Inkspire: Supporting Design Exploration with Generative AI through Analogical Sketching
candidates.authors: Lin, Kang, Martelaro, Kittur, Chen, Hong
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems, 1-18
candidates.task: product design concept prototyping with T2I and analogical sketching
candidates.evidence: Within-subjects study comparing Inkspire, a sketch-driven analogical T2I tool, with ControlNet; designers got more inspiration and explored more design ideas with Inkspire (AI-configuration comparison; outcomes mostly process and perception).

candidates.title: InkIdeator: Supporting Chinese-Style Visual Design Ideation via AI-Infused Exploration of Chinese Paintings
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems, 1-21
candidates.task: Chinese-style visual design ideation
candidates.evidence: Within-subjects study (N=12) comparing InkIdeator, an MLLM-based ideation system, with a baseline lacking dimensional keywords; outcomes concern creative ideation support and exploration, likely self-reported.

candidates.title: ProductMeta: An Interactive System for Metaphorical Product Design Ideation with Multimodal Large Language Models
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems, 1-24
candidates.task: metaphorical product design ideation (novice designers)
candidates.evidence: User studies of ProductMeta, a multimodal-LLM creativity support tool; reports that novice designers generated more diverse and contextually relevant design ideas. Comparison condition not described in the abstract.

candidates.title: Leveraging LLMs for Design Ideation: An AI Tool to Assist Creativity
candidates.venue: Responsible and Resilient Design for Society, Vol. 4 (ICoRD 2025), Lecture Notes in Mechanical Engineering, 579-589
candidates.task: small-group design ideation with a speech-based LLM agent
candidates.evidence: Compared AI-assisted ideation sessions using an analogical LLM ideation agent (ALIA) with traditional ideation sessions; participants rated their own ideas higher with the agent (self-ratings; sample size not given in the abstract).

candidates.title: The Effect of AI Integration on Designers' Creativity in the Sketching Process for Design Ideation
candidates.venue: Korea Institute of Design Research Society 9(4), 75-86
candidates.task: sketch-based design ideation (traditional vs ChatGPT-4/DALL-E)
candidates.evidence: Designers ideated with traditional sketch tools or with AI tools (ChatGPT-4, DALL-E); independent-samples t-tests found higher creativity scores for the AI group. Crossref lists the society as a corporate author.

candidates.title: Integrating AIGC into product design ideation teaching: An empirical study on self-efficacy and learning outcomes
candidates.task: product design ideation teaching
candidates.evidence: Title indicates an empirical study of integrating AIGC into product design ideation teaching with self-efficacy and learning outcomes; abstract not retrieved, so whether design creativity was rated is unconfirmed.

candidates.title: Exploration vs. Fixation: Scaffolding Divergent and Convergent Thinking for Human-AI Co-Creation with Generative Models
candidates.task: poster image creation (HAICo vs ChatGPT)
candidates.evidence: Within-subjects study (N=24) on a poster image creation task comparing HAICo, a GenAI system with switchable divergent and convergent modes, against ChatGPT; HAICo outperformed on several creativity and usability dimensions.

candidates.title: Understanding Design Fixation in Generative AI
candidates.authors: Chen, Song, Zheng, Jing, Hansen, Sun
candidates.task: design fixation of text and image generation models
candidates.evidence: Proposes a framework for generative-AI design fixation and reports an experimental study of how text and image models fixate on familiar solutions; mainly about model outputs, with the human role unclear.

candidates.title: Brief2Design: A Multi-phased, Compositional Approach to Prompt-based Graphic Design
candidates.task: prompt-based graphic design from client briefs
candidates.evidence: Within-subjects study with 12 designers comparing Brief2Design, a structured multi-phase prompt-based design tool, with a conversational baseline; the structured tool increased prompt diversity but achieved comparable image diversity.

candidates.title: Incentives shape how humans co-create with generative AI
candidates.task: creative writing with interactive AI under different incentives
candidates.evidence: Pre-registered randomized trial in which all participants could use AI; incentives were randomized (originality relative to peers vs quality), and originality incentives produced collectively more diverse writing. Outside the design lane; the randomized factor is incentives, not AI access.
